question: A compliance lead is writing an internal FAQ explaining how staff may use Claude. Which statement about model training is accurate to include?
options: A) Inputs and outputs from commercial products are used for training unless an organisation owner opts the account out.
B) Training behaviour is the same on personal and commercial plans, so a single sentence can cover every account type.
C) Inputs and outputs from commercial products such as Claude for Work are not used to train models by default.
D) Personal Free, Pro and Max accounts never contribute any conversation content to model training under any circumstance.
correct_answers: C) Inputs and outputs from commercial products such as Claude for Work are not used to train models by default.
explanations: This reverses the commercial default; the commercial position is that data is not used for training unless the customer opts in.
Consumer and commercial rules differ, and conflating them is the most common error an FAQ like this can make.
Correct. Commercial products do not use customer inputs and outputs for model training by default, which is the distinction staff most often get wrong.
On consumer plans the user chooses, and content can be used for model improvement if that setting is enabled, so 'never' is wrong.
